name: Individualist anarchism
summary: Individualist anarchism puts the sovereign individual above state, society and tradition, and holds that government is invasion to be replaced by voluntary association. In its American form it combines equal liberty, occupancy-and-use land titles, free competition and mutual banking, aiming to end rent, interest and profit by abolishing state monopolies. Its egoist strand follows Stirner in denying that the individual owes anything to the state, morality or any collective.
scope: Mainly the American individualist anarchism of Josiah Warren, Lysander Spooner and Benjamin Tucker (1850s-1900s), whose texts supply most answers, with Max Stirner's egoism as a second strand. The European illegalist and communist-leaning individualists and the Naturian fringe are noted but not the basis. Libertarian and anarcho-capitalist descendants are excluded.

furtherReading.note: Scholarly introduction to the egoist strand.

furtherReading.title: No Treason: The Constitution of No Authority (Spooner)
furtherReading.note: A founding American individualist argument that government needs individual consent.

furtherReading.title: Individual Liberty (Benjamin Tucker)
furtherReading.note: Tucker's essays from Liberty, including State Socialism and Anarchism.

keyFigures.name: Benjamin Tucker
keyFigures.role: Editor of Liberty and the leading theorist of American individualist anarchism.

keyFigures.name: Lysander Spooner
keyFigures.role: Author of No Treason, arguing that the Constitution binds no one who did not consent.

keyFigures.name: Max Stirner
keyFigures.role: Author of The Ego and Its Own, source of egoist anarchism.

sources.usedFor: State, taxation, land, money, interest, competition, religion, vice, marriage and violence.

sources.usedFor: Strands, key figures, American versus European currents, violence and markets.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Tucker wanted medicine left to free choice with no medical monopoly, and opposed tax-funded state provision; care is bought or mutually organised.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Tucker held wages would rise through free competition and cheap credit, not state wage-setting, which is coercive interference in contracts.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Tucker demanded universal competition as the cure for usury, rent and profit, though he rejected monopoly capitalism and some strands are market-socialist.

public-ownership.rationale: Tucker criticised state socialism as a new despotism and defined government as invasion; state ownership of industry is the opposite of his programme.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tucker called compulsory taxation the foundation of state monopoly and aggression, so higher taxes on anyone are rejected; he sought to abolish privilege instead.

unions-good.rationale: Voluntary combination of workers fits individualist principles and Tucker wanted labour to win its full product, but he distrusted coercion in strikes and Stirnerians distrust collectives; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property earned by labour and held by occupancy and use is defended by the American natural-law strand, but Tucker rejected inherent rights and Stirner treated property as might, so not a strong +2.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Tucker blamed corporate power on state-granted monopolies (money, land, tariffs, patents) and would remove them rather than add regulation, which is itself state action.

cut-welfare.rationale: Tax-funded welfare rests on compulsory taxation, which Tucker rejected; voluntary mutual aid replaces it, though adherents would not blame the poor for the monopoly system.

worker-ownership.rationale: Mutualist individualists favoured workers receiving their full product and cooperation by choice, but not a collective ownership requirement; Tucker's view was individual possession and free choice.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Government surveillance is an invasion of the non-invasive individual, which Tucker defined as the essence of the state; Stirner likewise denies any claim of the state over the individual.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Tucker said the state should not suppress vice and that none may dictate diet or health practices; adults live as they choose.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Individualists oppose legal restriction of expression and any external will imposed on non-invasive conduct; inferred from the rule of equal liberty.

strong-leader.rationale: Anarchists reject rulers entirely; Stirner calls every state a despotism whether the despot is one or many.

state-harmful.rationale: Tucker defined the state as the embodiment of invasion and sought its abolition; Stirner called every state a despotism.

limit-guns.rationale: Individualists hold each person's natural right to defend themselves; Spooner affirms the right to defend one's own rights, and gun laws impose an external will.

empower-police-military.rationale: Tucker wanted protection bought voluntarily rather than imposed by taxed state forces, so more state police and military authority is opposed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Tucker held that the state should not suppress vice and that love relations should be free; consensual adult exchange is not invasion.

decide-locally.rationale: Individualists prefer the smallest unit, ultimately the individual, and voluntary association; they would reject both national and local government as coercion, so only a mild yes.

rehabilitation.rationale: Tucker favoured gentleness with the corrigible and force only against incorrigible invaders, but the issue of prison aims was little treated; adherents are mixed.

traditional-family.rationale: Tucker called legal marriage absurd and wanted free, varied love relations; Stirner saw family ties as binding the individual.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Individualists object to legal marriage altogether, so the demand for state recognition does not fit, yet they would oppose banning it; neither side captures their view.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from self-ownership and Tucker's view that children belong to the mother until they can belong to themselves.

more-religion-public.rationale: Tucker defended freedom to believe and opposed religious monopoly, and personally was atheist; Stirner treated religion as subordination to spirit.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Tucker opposed invasion by anyone, but state programmes to correct past injustice require taxation and coercion; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The classic texts say little on this; Stirner's rejection of fixed essences points one way, but the question was not addressed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Individualists rank the individual above nation and tradition; Stirner treats such collective ideals as claims over the ego; inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Mutualists expected evolution through experiment, but the statement also asks respect for established institutions, which they reject; split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Restricting peaceful movement and association is invasion on equal-liberty grounds; no state may decide who may come.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: More power for a supranational state is more invasion; individualists reject all governments.

free-trade.rationale: Tucker opposed tariffs as monopoly privilege and demanded freedom of trade, but denied that capitalist profit benefits everyone; the claim is about trade itself.

nation-first.rationale: Individualists reject nations as collective claims on the individual, though they also reject global governance; the statement is a nationalist framing they do not share.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: State force abroad is funded by taxation and runs against opposition to state coercion, though Tucker allowed force to stop invaders; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Borders are state creations that interfere with peaceful movement and exchange; inferred from equal liberty and no-state premises.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; imposing limits would take state coercion, while individualists favour free economic activity.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Drastic government action means coercive state power; individualists would address harms through property rights and liability rather than state programmes; anachronistic.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents of progress through free enterprise lean one way, the Naturians another.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents would oppose subsidy but not the power source, and no stance is documented.

revolution-justified.rationale: Tucker justified violence to resist invasion; the European illegalist strand embraced it, while Stirner and mutualists expected evolution; majority yes.

experts-over-public.rationale: Anything giving a class authority over individual conduct is rejected; Godwin opposed any authority over individual judgment.

central-planning.rationale: Tucker rejected state socialism for giving the majority unlimited control over conduct and demanded free competition.

socialized-markets.rationale: Many American individualists were market socialists, favouring markets with labour receiving its full product, but they would not require worker or public ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tucker explicitly rejected the single tax: rent arises from land monopoly, which should be abolished rather than taxed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: All compulsory taxation is rejected as aggression, so heavy inheritance taxes are too.

basic-income.rationale: A state-paid income requires compulsory taxation, which Tucker called the foundation of state aggression.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tucker described tariffs as a monopoly privilege he called misusury and demanded their abolition.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of investment contradicts the free competition and abolition of state monopoly that Tucker demanded.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Tucker expected ending monopolies to disperse capital and land among occupant-users, but he favoured no state action to ensure it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Individualists wanted labour to receive its full product through free exchange and mutual banks, not abolition of money or wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Tucker attacked the money monopoly as the chief support of interest and proposed free competing mutual banks in place of state banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages and prices is state control; Tucker wanted competition with no monopoly.

one-party-rule.rationale: Anarchists reject any ruling party; Tucker held the test of anarchism is refusing to impose will on others by force.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: All hereditary or other rulers are rejected as government by external will.

democracy-best.rationale: Tucker rejected majority rule as absolute and wrote of the futility of the ballot; Spooner said majorities afford no guarantees for justice.

direct-votes.rationale: Majority votes still impose will on non-consenting individuals, so direct democracy is not an answer, though it beats representation in being less distant; Spooner says majorities guarantee no justice.

workers-councils.rationale: Council rule is collective political power over individuals; European individualists rejected workers as a class base and syndicalism's focus.

right-to-secede.rationale: Spooner held the Constitution binds only those who consented and defended Southern secession; Thoreau claimed a right of disunion; the individual may withdraw.

natural-rulers.rationale: Anarchists deny that any person has authority over another; Godwin opposed all authority over individual judgment.

political-violence-never.rationale: Tucker justified violence against invasion and incorrigible invaders, though he preferred persuasion; European individualists went further; pacifism is not the position.

war-builds-character.rationale: War is state action funded by taxation and conscription; Tucker saw no merit in it, and Stirner scorns sacrifice to collective causes.

separate-church-state.rationale: Tucker opposed religious monopolies and any external power dictating belief; separation is the minimum of that stance.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: No law imposed on non-invasive conduct is accepted, and Tucker was atheist and defended freedom of belief.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Tucker wanted protection of person and property bought or organised voluntarily rather than state-run; Spooner affirmed each person's right to defend rights and aid others.

military-superiority.rationale: Maintaining a state military through taxation is rejected outright.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nations as collective bodies are rejected in favour of the individual; Stirner scorns belonging to any group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: European individualists rejected the bourgeois and proletarian divide as a capitalist construct; Tucker blamed monopoly privilege, not class war as history's engine.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Tucker stood for equal liberty, not equal results, and held that labour's wage is its own product, which varies.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Occupancy-and-use land titles support those who actually use land, but collective authority is not an individualist idea; not addressed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations would be extracted by taxation from people not personally guilty; individualists tie liability to actual invaders; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political unions of peoples mean larger states; individualists reject states and group belonging.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Stirner's egoism holds the individual owes nothing to others and prizes autonomy; Tucker rejects inherent moral duties, though not all strands call selfishness good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Tucker said obligations exist only when consciously assumed; Stirner says we owe each other nothing.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The Naturian strand valued nature, while Tucker and Stirner treat value as individually assigned; split and little addressed.

limit-population.rationale: State population control is coercion; Tucker held parental rights should not be taken away; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The Naturian strand prefigured primitivism but mainstream American individualists wanted a freed market economy; minority view.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not documented; disruption of institutions would be welcomed, but the statement carries no stated individualist position.

human-enhancement.rationale: Individualists defend each person's free choice over their own body and health practices; inferred from Tucker's opposition to dictating health practices.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Putting more decisions in any government, algorithmic or not, extends external will over individuals.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Privacy against state intrusion fits non-invasion and anarchist hostility to state power; anachronistic but clear by inference.

restore-past-order.rationale: Individualists seek a new order of equal liberty or individual autonomy; Stirner rejects ideals that bind the ego, past or future.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Anarchists hold their principle of non-invasion as a test, not subject to results; Tucker offers a simple test of anarchism.

direct-action.rationale: Tucker favoured passive but organised refusal to pay taxes and mutual banks in defiance of law, while calling the ballot futile.

means-match-ends.rationale: Tucker's mutual banks, voluntary association and refusal of the ballot are chosen as means consistent with a free society; Stirner expected collapse as egoism spreads.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Only the Naturian fringe leaned this way; the mainstream wanted free markets and exchange.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Individualists favoured market exchange between specialised producers; Godwin even disliked cooperative labour but did not seek abolishing division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: American individualists preferred market-based distribution to need-based distribution, and labour's full product to communist sharing.

production-for-use.rationale: Individualists want production through free exchange, which can include profit-seeking, though Tucker wanted profit eliminated by competition; not framed this way.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Tucker argued interest, profit and rent are tribute made possible by monopoly and fall away with free banking, and labour's natural wage is its full product.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dictatorial class power is the imposition of one will over others that Tucker's test of anarchism excludes.

collective-farming.rationale: Land is held by individual occupancy and use; collectivisation by compulsion is invasion, and Stirner opposes belonging to a collective.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not an individualist thesis; Tucker blamed state monopoly rather than markets, and war is a state activity either way.

taxation-theft.rationale: Tucker called compulsory taxation the foundation of state monopoly and aggression and urged organised refusal to pay; Spooner makes consent of each contributor necessary.

harm-principle.rationale: Tucker's equal liberty permits restraint only of invasion, but he rejected the notion that the state may restrict even then; they would say no state at all.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Natural-law individualists put rights in each person, though Tucker and Stirner reject inherent rights; they agree that no group holds claims over the individual.

conscription.rationale: Forced service is the plain subjection of a non-invasive individual to an external will.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Spooner and Thoreau stressed consent and withdrawal from the state, and Tucker called the ballot futile; exit comparison itself not drawn.

state-as-business.rationale: Individualists want no state, so running one like a business is not the aim, though competition and withdrawal chime with it; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Tucker defined liberty as the absence of invasion; material provision through the state would require taxation he rejected.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; anarchists see state power as dominant, yet this claim is not documented.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; the individual is stressed over group categories, so adherents would reject group-based judgement.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation by any corporate body is a rule over individuals; Tucker rejects political representation and the ballot.

total-state.rationale: The state directing every area of life is the opposite of the anarchist position.

national-rebirth.rationale: Collective national projects are claims over the individual that Stirner rejects.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Territorial expansion is state aggression funded by taxation.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority resting on oaths between lords and followers is rule, which anarchists reject; Stirner denies any duty to keep promises.

bound-labor.rationale: Forced labour owed to a lord is the clearest invasion of the individual.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed by sources; Stirner's rejection of fixed spirits points slightly to scepticism but is not a programme.

universal-morality.rationale: Tucker rejected inherent moral rights and duties and Stirner rejected morality as fixed obligation; the natural-law strand dissents.

single-common-good.rationale: Stirner rejects ideals above the individual, and Tucker's equal liberty has no single common good beyond non-invasion.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Individualists reject states and national claims, though they would not deny individuals the right to settle; inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: A state-granted right of citizenship is not an individualist concept, although they do not oppose individual return; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: State language policy imposes will through taxation and law; inferred from opposition to state action.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic control by the public or all workers over firms denies the owner's freedom; voluntary arrangements among owners are fine; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Vouchers are tax-funded and the state remains the funder, so they reject them, though they would prefer them to state schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Both stimulus and deficits are state acts; individualists reject state fiscal management itself, not taking either side.

economic-freedom.rationale: Tucker held political liberty needs free competition in money, land and trade, though he saw economic freedom as ending capitalist privilege.

rule-by-example.rationale: Anarchists reject rulers rather than want them to be better examples; Godwin hoped for benevolence yet not government.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nations as units are not recognised; the right of the individual to secede is, per Spooner, which may support smaller groups; mixed.

force-without-un.rationale: State force abroad is rejected whatever the authorisation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Egoists reject God and moral rules as authorities and Tucker was an atheist, but Stirner distrusted reason as another spirit, so not strongly.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare is rejected, and so the allocation by citizenship has no support, yet it is not a position they discuss.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Tax-funded welfare is rejected; conditions on it are secondary and not discussed.

class-collaboration.rationale: Free exchange between individuals is fine, but European individualists rejected class concepts and Tucker saw capitalism as tribute; split.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not documented; destroying institutions by force is invasion unless they are owned by the destroyers, though Stirner scorns reverence.

dominated-front.rationale: State blocs are rejected, and Stirner's rejection of belonging to collectives applies.

workers-nation.rationale: Neither nation nor class as a collective is the base; European individualists rejected the proletariat as construct.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Legal role distinctions are an external will imposed on individuals; Tucker wanted love relations free and varied.

ban-interest.rationale: Tucker called interest usury but wanted it abolished by competition in free banking, not by legal prohibition.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Laws forcing separation impose will on peaceful people, the core of what Tucker calls invasion.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Individualists see the state as maintaining monopolies of money, land and tariffs for privileged owners, though they see it as invasion per se, not only class rule.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents would oppose subsidies and favour no state policy on production.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Demanding that people give up their culture is imposition of external will; Stirner rejects belonging.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not an individualist idea and opposed to open association; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: They reject the ballot as futile, although preferring a fairer scheme would not matter.

national-mission.rationale: A state spreading its government abroad is aggression.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The European strand was tied to anarcha-feminism and Tucker opposed legal marriage control; the structural claim is inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anarchists see rulers as beneficiaries of privilege and the state as invasion; Stirner calls every state despotism.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: State control over reproduction violates the individual and parental rights Tucker upheld.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Anarchists hold that state agents are liable for invasion and Spooner defends redress of wrongs by individuals; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Tucker and Spooner reject even a minimal tax-funded state, though it is nearer to them than larger ones; this is the minarchist rival.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Discouraging unions of people by social engineering is interference; Tucker wanted love relations free.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Tucker's equal liberty gives every person the same sovereignty, but Tucker and Stirner reject inherent moral rights, so not a strong yes.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist question that individualists do not address.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed; they reject all states, but the particular claim about settler colonialism is not documented.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Uniform state civil law would be another monopoly of legal authority, though they also oppose religious law imposed on individuals; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Tucker defended freedom of belief and no external power over choice of priest.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Banning slaughter imposes a will on non-invasive conduct, as Tucker said of diet and health practices.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: They would oppose state schools themselves, but if a state school exists they would object to compelled religious instruction; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Anarchists reject state strengthening in any circumstances.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Spooner demanded the separate individual consent of everyone made to contribute and called the Constitution void without it.

trade-surplus.rationale: Tucker favoured free trade, and state aims for surpluses are mercantilist.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced expulsion is plain invasion of non-invasive people.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Tucker's test of anarchism is refusing to impose will on others by force, and the American strand stresses non-aggression.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Tucker demanded universal competition and said it drives down usury, though he did not frame it as struggle between peoples; the statement joins both.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Outlawing parties is state suppression of non-invasive speech and association.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: They define liberty as the absence of invasion, and domination without interference may not count; the republican concept is not addressed.

separated-powers.rationale: Checking states against one another is better than concentration, but all state powers remain invasion; Spooner finds the Constitution void.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined party leading others is rule by a minority, anathema to individualists.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Priority in law implies compulsory redistribution; Tucker expected the poor to gain by ending monopoly, not state favour.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing itself is a state matter; they would favour ending it or transferring to occupants, but the framing is not documented.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Tucker said force in strikes is a matter to be judged by invasion, not legal restriction; the state may not impose conditions on voluntary action.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Tucker blamed poverty on monopoly privilege in money, land and tariffs, not on population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Group cohesion as a goal is not an individualist value; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Lotteries still fill state offices; Tucker rejects the state, although a lottery is less objectionable than election; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Suspending protections is state aggression, and Spooner says a government resting on force has no consent.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price-fixing is state interference in exchange, and Tucker wanted free competition.

party-controls-media.rationale: State control of information is an invasion of non-invasive expression.

party-commands-army.rationale: Any state army is rejected, and a party-commanded one is worse.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: State-made conditions on citizenship have no standing for those who reject the state; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: They reject representation itself, so pay level for representatives is not an issue.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding members to collective decisions subordinates the individual; Stirner's unions of egoists are renewed by will.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Bigger states are no improvement, and sovereignty belongs to the individual, per Spooner on consent.

head-commands-forces.rationale: State commanders of forces and ministers are rulers, rejected.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Hierarchies claiming authority over the individual conscience are rejected, and Tucker opposed religious monopoly.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by clerics is rule, and Tucker opposed religious monopoly.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not an individualist thesis, which treats war as state action to be refused by withholding taxes; adherents may choose either way.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Tucker said the state should not suppress vice and adults may live as they choose.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: They reject the office, so term limits are indifferent.

recall-officials.rationale: They reject the state and the ballot, so recall mechanics are not their concern.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anarchists oppose military alliances and standing forces abroad, though their aim is to abolish the state, not only alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Banning rent is a legal prohibition of voluntary contracts, and Tucker expected rent to shrink naturally once land monopoly ended.

people-in-arms.rationale: Individuals defending themselves fits Spooner's right of defence and replaces state armies, though the idea is not a stated programme.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Only the Naturians held this, and the mainstream is indifferent.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunifying states is no aim of anti-state thinkers; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed; individualists emphasise individuals over cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Tucker allowed force against incorrigible invaders, but execution by a tax-funded state for crimes like terrorism is state power they reject; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curricula in state schools are rejected, so they would not want the state to add content; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: State schooling imposed on citizens is rejected, and atheist-leaning individualists would not favour compelled creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Tucker said the state should not suppress vice, and adults may choose.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are state matters; they favour individual consent over inherited allegiance, per Spooner.

minority-language-support.rationale: Tax-funded language support is rejected, though they favour free language use.

religious-exemptions.rationale: They want no general laws burdening anyone, so exemptions for some would be a poor second-best; split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Stirner prizes autonomy and rejects binding social ties, while Tucker rejected inherent duty; inferred from Mill-like temper.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose state debts, which are paid by taxation, but cancellation by states is a policy question outside their sources.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Tucker held political liberty requires ending monopolies in money, land and tariffs, not only abolishing the state.

constituent-assembly.rationale: A fresh constitution by an assembly still binds non-consenting people, per Spooner.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberty is the condition of order, per Tucker, so none may be restricted for growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: State aid is funded by taxation, which is rejected, though voluntary charity is not opposed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: State armaments paid by taxation are rejected.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Electing a ruler is no cure; the ballot is futile, per Tucker.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Tucker wanted central banking and the money monopoly abolished for free competing banks.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: A state's claim to land as a historic homeland has no meaning for anti-state thinkers, who would favour occupants' titles.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is justified by labour and occupancy and use, not by service to a common good, and Stirner calls property unlimited dominion.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Individualists reject the Soviet state but the classification was not their debate.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Acting before harm is shown conflicts with a non-invasion test; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Collective defence is a state treaty system; individuals defend themselves and those wronged, per Spooner.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Anarchists do not recognise states' claims, so the legal question is not theirs, though an annexation without consent is hostile to Spooner's consent test.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Subordinating clergy to state authority is more state power; Tucker wanted all monopolies abolished, religious ones included.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A head of state of any kind is a ruler, rejected.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Spooner defended Southern secession and said the Constitution binds no one who did not consent.

region-keeps-system.rationale: This concerns state arrangements they do not address; they would favour autonomy but not the larger state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The sacralising of a ruler is the reverse of Stirner's rejection of spooks and of anarchism.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Any income tax is compulsory taxation, which Tucker called aggression.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; Stirner's egoism points to self-creation but is not a thesis about upbringing.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A ruler is rejected, and they hold that law needs consent, per Spooner.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutions are void without consent, says Spooner, whatever their mix.

leader-cult.rationale: Stirner mocks the elevation of any person or cause above the ego.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; Tucker said children belong to their mothers until old enough to own themselves, which cuts against presumed equality but courts would not decide.

land-redistribution.rationale: Tucker wanted titles by occupancy and use and the end of land monopoly, but not state seizure and gift; some would accept returning land to users.

refugee-return.rationale: Property rights of those expelled and free movement favour return, inferred from non-aggression.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: State claims to territory by nationality are rejected as aggression.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing change of belief invades non-invasive individuals.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compelled dress is an external will over a non-invasive person.

common-currency.rationale: Tucker wanted competing private money against monopoly money; a state-run common currency is another monopoly.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Political unions based on ancestry are state projects and group belonging that Stirner rejects.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: They reject collective bodies holding authority over individuals, though minority self-government is milder than a state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A question of nationalist strategy not addressed; they favour individual freedom to move or stay.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Tucker blamed monopoly privilege politically, while Stirner stressed ideas as ruling; the statement is Marxist and not accepted, though the economic side is partly shared.

ban-cartels.rationale: Tucker blamed monopolies on state privilege and wanted competition, not an antitrust state, which would be another state act.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are tax-funded privilege to banks, and Tucker wanted the money monopoly removed and competition universal.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: They reject both courts and majorities as authorities over individuals; Spooner says majorities guarantee no justice.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Mandated public quotas are state rule and public bodies are rejected.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Closed economic blocs shut trade, which Tucker called monopoly and wanted free.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards imposed by states on trade are state regulation, rejected, though Tucker did not oppose free exchange.

moral-incentives.rationale: Tucker rejected inherent duties, and Stirner says we owe each other nothing; labour is paid its full product.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The European illegalist strand favoured propaganda of the deed, but Tucker and mutualists expected evolution and Stirner collapse; mainstream no.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Tucker wanted all state-granted privileges ended and Stirner called any state despotism; titles are legal privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred: the individual, not nation or civilization, is the centre of this ideology, and Stirner rejected national causes as 'spooks'.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule over others without their consent is invasion; Spooner's consent argument and Tucker's equal liberty rule it out whatever the stated aim.

patriotic-education.rationale: Tucker opposed state schooling and Spooner denied any duty to the state; Stirner treated the nation as a spook.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: state-imposed preferences violate equal liberty, though private discrimination would be tolerated and the issue is anachronistic.

public-money-creation.rationale: Tucker's mutual banking called for free competition in issuing money and an end to the legal money monopoly.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed directly; they blamed state monopolies for capitalism's ills, which suggests no collapse but also no endorsement of existing capitalism, so inferred as split.

former-empire-influence.rationale: State projection of influence is a coercive use of government, which they rejected on principle.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: they backed free competition and opposed tariffs as monopoly, but also wanted trade without state capital, so delinking by policy is unwelcome.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: Tucker saw workers everywhere as exploited by state-backed monopolies of land, money and credit, which is against the thesis.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Voluntary association is central and state coercion illegitimate, so owners may choose partners; a few adherents objected to the outcomes, hence not +2.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Spooner argued the Constitution binds no one without individual consent, and anarchists rejected state-held guarantees of rights, though he used natural law against government.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Spooner argued the Constitution and treaties bind no one who never consented, so an imposed treaty has no force; this is inferred from that consent principle.

elective-rulers.rationale: Anarchists reject rulers altogether and hold that an election confers no authority over non-voters, so neither inheritance nor election is endorsed.

minority-veto.rationale: Spooner's No Treason holds that no majority can bind an individual who has not consented, which is the core of the consent argument.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Spooner held that government acting beyond its own legal limits has no authority and may be resisted, though adherents deny that any ruler is legitimate in the first place.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Individualist anarchists reject legislatures as invaders of equal liberty, so no assembly should be supreme lawmaker.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Stirnerian egoists deny that animals or anyone hold moral claims, while some natural-law and naturist individualists stressed animal welfare; adherents are split.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animals count as property that owners may use under equal liberty; inferred from the property doctrine, with no stated humane duty.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Obligations are voluntary contracts; Stirner denies any duty owed by rank, and charity is a free choice rather than a class duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Tucker urged abstention from voting and Stirner scorned political causes, but Tucker also ran a propaganda journal, so the withdrawal is partial; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Stirner and Tucker held that state, church and schools shape docile subjects; the statement is a broader media critique inferred from that.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Stirner holds the state rests on belief in 'spooks' that subjects accept, and Spooner holds that force is dressed up as consent; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Tucker located exploitation in four domestic state monopolies (land, money, tariff, patents), not in a global transfer of surplus.

native-born-offices.rationale: Individualist anarchists want no public offices at all and hold that birth confers no political standing; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Individualists reject any party or authority directing others, so no party answers to another; inferred, since the statement concerns communist parties.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Tucker favoured free trade and free exchange of capital, but opposed state-run aid; free investment is not rejected.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Individualist anarchists reject states and their borders and condemned war, so recovering lost territory is not a legitimate aim.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal liberty applies to individuals, so no group by descent may hold political rule over another.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Individualist anarchists oppose constitutions as such (Spooner), so they would not make anything a constitutional founding value; they do oppose fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Tucker opposed state socialism as much as other forms of state power; fascism came later, so this is inferred from their opposition to the state.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Spooner wrote against slavery and No Treason addresses the Civil War, treating slavery as the issue, though he also denied the Union's legitimacy.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Taxpayer-funded monuments would be opposed as state spending, though privately owned ones are fine; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Public programmes are opposed on principle, so state attention to either sex is rejected; inferred from opposition to state services.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Aggression is wrong whatever the sex of the victim, but protection is to be provided voluntarily, not by state services; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: They reject government wholesale and favour voluntary institutions varying by community, so no form is universal; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army is an arm of the state that equal liberty condemns, and individualist anarchists opposed standing armies and conscription.

paid-care-work.rationale: Market wages for care contracted freely are fine, but state wages for housework are opposed; adherents have no common line.

filial-duty.rationale: Tucker held obligations exist only when assumed, so lifelong duty is a matter of choice; inferred, with low confidence.

office-by-exam.rationale: Individualist anarchists reject the state and any official posts, whether by election, examination or patronage; inferred from that.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: With no state, there is no authority to block voluntary sales; inferred from their rejection of government.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Marriage is a voluntary contract that parties may end; Tucker and Warren defended free love and rejected state marriage law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Individualists reject representation and rule by majority, so no leaders to bind or recall; adherents answer neither way.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private, voluntary saving fits their view, but they would oppose any state mandate; mildly yes, inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: They held land titles rest on occupancy and use, but individuals held it, not the community or nation; partly agrees.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: They opposed taxation and state spending altogether, so a budget process is not a safeguard they seek; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: A state-imposed common language is coercion; inferred from rejection of state schooling and public monopolies.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Occupancy-and-use titles do not depend on nationality, and they rejected the state power to exclude; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Individualists treat only invasion by a person as a wrong, so outcome-based tests have no place; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed; Stirner and Tucker did not condemn consumption, and adherents are split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Individualists oppose state coercion and war funding by taxation; inferred from Spooner on state wrongdoing.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Alliances and blocs are state affairs and intervention is invasion; inferred from the doctrine of equal liberty.

corporate-influence.rationale: Tucker blamed state-granted monopolies and privileges for exploitation, so state-corporate favouritism is a target, though the remedy is abolishing the state, not regulating money.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Individualist anarchists reject state interference in voluntary exchange and association, including controlling who may give or receive money.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: They opposed taxation as theft and any state role in family life, so state payments for births are rejected.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of political authority; a local government restricting sales conflicts with equal liberty, though occupancy-and-use land titles are favoured.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state-run employer financed by taxation is invasion in their view; work comes from free competition and mutual banking.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; they distrusted majority rule and states as such, and would not see democracy promotion as a route to peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Spooner argued that no contract binds anyone to the state and Stirner denied any duty to law or morality, so obligations arise only from consent.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from their denial that any state has legitimate authority over its subjects, so none has a right to rule another; they favoured defensive force against invasion.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed; as free association and competition, they would leave workers to organise as they choose rather than prescribe a form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred from their equal-liberty and egoist principles, which give no basis for blaming a minority collectively.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Tucker and other individualists held that marriage should be a private contract with no state licence or privileges, and favoured free love.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed; they wanted the state abolished, so a legal access right to its records has little role, though secrecy by the state would be distrusted.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; free competition would decide where goods are made, so they are indifferent between local and distant production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's union of egoists and voluntary association, which favour small, informal, consent-based groups over fixed organisations.

national-law-over-international.rationale: They reject the state's legal authority at every level; Spooner held that constitutions bind no one, so national law gets no special precedence.

religious-nation.rationale: They were generally freethinkers who treated religion as a private matter and rejected state or collective definitions of belonging.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the sovereign-individual rejection of state hierarchy; no state is owed deference.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: taxation is rejected altogether, so revenue pooling between regions does not arise and the school is indifferent.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Tucker defended individual ownership of the product of labour and rejected common ownership of land and tools.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: Tucker opposed state socialism and communist anarchism by argument, but non-aggression rules out a campaign of force.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Tucker treated taxation as theft, so a publicly funded system of any provider mix is rejected.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred: Tucker was an atheist and Stirner treated religion as a spook, though neither held to the material-conditions explanation.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Tucker blamed state-backed monopolies in land, money and credit for exploitation and saw free competition as the remedy, not capitalism as a stage.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: Tucker sought equal liberty for women through ending legal monopolies and marriage law, not a transformed economy.

socialized-care.rationale: Tucker rejected compulsory taxation and public provision; care is bought or mutually organised.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's individual sovereignty over nation and tradition, and Tucker's opposition to coercive policy.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: Spooner held that no agreement binds those who have not consented, so state treaties have no standing.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Warren's and Tucker's order rests on individual sovereignty and individual titles, not communal property.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: state-steered settlement is government coercion and subsidy, which the school rejects.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Tucker called anarchism a socialism distinct from both state socialism and monopoly capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Occupancy-and-use land titles rest on present use, not historical or religious ties, so ancestral claims create no title.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed by the texts; an adherent would accept the historical record.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Victimless sexual acts between adults are the individual's own business under equal liberty, so the state has no right to punish them.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Government is itself invasion; suppressing opposition and associations is the clearest case of it.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Spooner, Tucker and Stirner all denied the state any authority over belief or worship.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Spooner's No Treason holds that the state has no rightful authority over anyone, so ruling distant peoples for profit is more so invasion.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; the individualists opposed state wars but would accept voluntary defence of home, and this religious obligation is not theirs.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Individualists deny that any ruler is legitimate, and they would not endorse forcing a religious test of rule; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Spooner and Tucker rejected majority rule as invasive and preferred voluntary association; the point of the statement, direct participation, fits only partly.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Individualists treated state privilege and monopoly as the root issue and focused on individual liberty; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Individualists oppose state-defined legal categories but support each person's freedom to define themselves; adherents would split on legal recognition.

assisted-dying.rationale: Self-ownership implies a right to end one's own life, so voluntary help is not for the state to forbid; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Tucker called himself a socialist and used left-wing arguments about exploitation, so the divide was not obsolete; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Tucker blamed state-backed monopolies for exploiting labor, while Stirner rejected alienation as a spook, so adherents split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed by the texts; individualists held no concept of cultural incompatibility and favoured voluntary association.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Spooner, Tucker and Stirner all denied that authority derives from God or people; Stirner called such ideas spooks.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from individual liberty, which would oppose forced dress rules though anarchists oppose state institutions generally.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anarchists uphold voluntary contract and would reject state regulation of contracts; inferred, and sympathetic to the complaint.

social-market-economy.rationale: Individualists wanted free competition and no state, including no state welfare; they sought to end privilege, not regulate markets.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Abolishing the state includes its army; Spooner's No Treason attacks the state's claim on citizens for war.

rich-first.rationale: Tucker's view is that equal liberty and abolition of monopoly give all an equal start; favoured groups getting rich first is the privilege he opposed.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Individualists opposed state wars and entanglements; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Individualist anarchists reject the state and any hereditary or other rulers, as Spooner and Tucker argued.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Tucker's mutual banking would issue credit at cost, abolishing interest through users' mutual banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anarchists oppose state power, so refusing outside lenders' terms is inferred, though they wanted no government to negotiate at all.

property-franchise.rationale: Spooner argued that voting shows no consent and individualists reject state authority, so no franchise is justified; the property restriction is inferred as disliked.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not addressed by the American individualists; Tucker backed women's equality but not this ecological claim.

reification.rationale: Tucker located exploitation in state monopolies and not in the social form of capitalism, so the thesis is inferred to be disliked.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Tucker blamed state-granted monopolies and held free competition would open the press, so the claim is inferred to be rejected.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Spooner favoured natural law applied by juries, but individualists reject state law; the statement presumes rulers, so no clear answer.

racial-franchise.rationale: Equal liberty for each individual excludes group-based political rights.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic and presupposes collective decisions; no position can be inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from distrust of state secrecy: if government exists, anarchists want it open to scrutiny.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Tucker opposed legal regulation of marriage and religion; this is stated in his writings.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Voluntary boycott is permitted, but individualists reject treating persons by group identity; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Individualists reject any collective body binding the individual, so an assembly deciding public questions conflicts with their view; Spooner's support for juries judging the law gives a partial exception, so only a mild no.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Egoists and Tucker-style individualists left belief to individual judgement and rejected authority over conscience; favouring reasoned rethinking of inherited doctrine is inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Tucker held that state monopolies in money, land, tariffs and patents concentrate wealth in few hands and that free competition would spread it.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: They opposed the state army and conscription, but held that no one should be barred from any activity by law, so the open-service principle is inferred as agreeable.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Stirner and Tucker saw state education as indoctrination and the state as having no claim to promote any belief, whether religious or atheist.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Tucker proposed replacing state police with voluntary defence and protective associations, and rejected state punishment as invasion.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: They reject both majority rule and state executive power, so a rule for sharing it among communities is outside their frame; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Tucker preferred free competition and voluntary mutual aid to state programs, though he saw charity as secondary to ending monopoly; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Tucker and Spooner rejected taking part in government, so term limits are beside the point and neither backed nor opposed.

vote-delegation.rationale: Spooner held that voting gives no consent and that the state has no legitimacy, so a system of delegated votes within it is rejected; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Policy priorities set by the state are not their approach; inferred from rejection of state-directed goals, and the issue is anachronistic.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious bodies are private voluntary associations to them, and Tucker backed equal rights for women; this makes the statement acceptable, inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Individualist anarchists opposed state marriage law and held that spouses are equal sovereign individuals; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Spooner and Tucker rejected voting as consent to the state, so extending it to anyone is not a goal; inferred from No Treason.

rent-control.rationale: Tucker held that free competition and ending state monopolies would end high rents; price caps by law would be state interference.

abolish-ip.rationale: Tucker defended patents and copyrights as a reward of labour, while Warren's cost principle was more doubtful; the mainstream strand kept them.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Stirner's egoism denies that the individual owes service to nation or any collective, and uniformed state drill is the opposite of free association.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from opposition to the state and its armaments, which Spooner treated as unconsented force.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from rejection of the state and standing armies; foreign armies are state forces the individual never consented to.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state authority, so state declarations of any kind carry no weight.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Tucker's labour theory of value held that rent, interest and profit are unearned and would vanish once state monopolies ended.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Equal liberty permits force in defence of person; Spooner justified resisting invasion of rights.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Stirner treats nation and similar collectives as 'spooks' with no claim over the individual.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic; Stirner rejects fixed essences as spooks but the school never took a stand on sex as construct.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from Stirner's rejection of fixed collective identities as binding on the unique individual.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Stirner mocks sacrificial devotion to nation or cause as a 'spook' to which the individual is not bound.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Stirner treats good and evil as fixed ideas; politics is about interests and the individual's own power.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; nation and homeland are not categories the strand uses.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the view that society and voluntary culture precede and can do without the state, which they sought to abolish.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic; Stirner was atheist and held God a spook, with no recorded view on its gendering.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anachronistic; religious texts hold no authority for Stirner, but the test the statement proposes is not his.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Rejecting group privilege and state power, they would allow no national majority claim on economic life.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of the state and its territorial administration.

independent-unions.rationale: Individualists wanted all association voluntary and free of the state, so unions would be independent of any government or party by definition.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Tucker called himself an anarchistic socialist but rejected rule by any class or majority; inferred from his opposition to all government.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Tucker opposed taxation and state monopolies, so water, hospitals and transport would be provided by competing private or mutual concerns, not public bodies.

second-chamber.rationale: Spooner denied that any legislature, let alone a bicameral one, has legitimate authority over individuals, so adding a chamber is not wanted.

municipal-property.rationale: Land and capital belong to individual occupiers and users under Warren and Tucker; collective local ownership is inferred to be rejected, though cooperative arrangements are allowed voluntarily.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from voluntarism: individualists favour contracts between individuals, not standing municipal confederations, though voluntary federations are not forbidden.

family-wage.rationale: Wages are set by free competition and contract in Tucker's view, so no norm of a family-supporting wage is imposed; inferred from his labour theory.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Tucker opposed state licensing of medicine; abolishing regulatory gatekeeping follows from his rejection of medical monopoly, though drug approval itself was not discussed.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from opposition to tax-funded government programs, though adherents would welcome privately funded life extension.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Tucker's mutual banking and rejection of state control of money and of government surveillance of voluntary exchange.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the individualist defence of privacy and voluntary association against state interference, and Stirner's refusal to owe anything to any collective.

person-over-state.rationale: The sovereign individual above the state is the core claim; Spooner denies the state any rightful claim over persons, and Stirner rejects all collective ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Stirner rejects 'spooks' and fixed ideas, and Tucker was an atheist who opposed religious authority; politics serving a spiritual nature is not an individualist aim.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Individualists reject national legislatures and regional governments alike, so the question of which can revoke the other has no adherent answer.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the individualist view that producers should be free to adopt technology without state prohibition.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; adherents would leave settlement patterns to individual choice rather than rank them.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Individualists treat the individual, not any group, as the political unit, and Stirner dismisses collective identities as fixed ideas.

racial-pride.rationale: Stirner dismissed pride in collective identities such as nation or race as spooks, though adherents would not forbid it; inferred from his critique of collectivities.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Spooner and Tucker allow force only in defence against invasion and aggression, and opposed state wars of conquest.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Stirner denied that the individual owes anything to any collective such as the nation, and Spooner rejected national loyalty as a basis for obligation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Spooner held that voting and representation bind no one and the state itself is illegitimate, so separate electorates are rejected along with the franchise.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Spooner denied that the state is a country with claims on the individual, so a plot against 'my country' is not an individualist concern.

free-public-college.rationale: Tucker opposed state education funded by taxation as invasion and wanted schooling left to voluntary association.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Spooner called taxation robbery; pollution harms are handled by liability to the victim, not by state levies.

future-generations.rationale: Stirner's egoism denies duties owed to any abstraction, though individuals may care voluntarily; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Individualists treated people as sovereign individuals, not as groups with shared values; Tucker backed women's equal liberty. Inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Individualist anarchists opposed standing state armies as instruments of invasion; the statement's national-safety clause is inferred to be tolerable.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Anarchists reject state treaties altogether, and secret ones are all the worse; inferred as mild agreement.

capital-controls.rationale: Tucker demanded free competition in banking and exchange and denounced state control of money as monopoly.

missingStatements.text: Land should belong to those who occupy and use it, not to absentee owners holding it by legal title.
missingStatements.rationale: Occupancy and use is the individualist anarchists' standard for land titles, with rent from monopoly seen as unjust.

missingStatements.text: Banking and the issuing of money should be open to free competition, with no legal monopoly.
missingStatements.rationale: Tucker's mutual banking aimed to end the money monopoly he saw as the root support of interest.

missingStatements.text: The only legitimate way to bind a person to a government or a contract is that person's own individual consent.
missingStatements.rationale: Spooner argued each contributor's separate consent is needed, and Tucker held obligations exist only when assumed.

notes: Stirnerian egoists deny natural rights and morality; the Spooner natural-law strand affirms them. European illegalists would answer revolution and violence questions more strongly yes. Tucker's text was read only in part (about the first 100,000 characters of a very long compilation).
